name: tin
description: Open-source marketing system, designed for coding agents.

paragraphs: Why would you invent marketing from first principles when you can use a battle-tested marketing stack in 10 minutes?
Now with 60 workflows you can use right away, across organic search, content, social, outreach, product QA, paid ads and creative work.

These are the main areas covered by the current catalog. Availability depends on the workflow's inputs, connected services, and operator settings. Some workflows run on demand; others can be saved with a schedule.
features: More workflows and connections. Extend product QA into fixes, add analytics sources such as GA4, take website changes beyond pages, and build out lifecycle marketing and more ad platforms. These need their own provider…
Better evaluation. Build workflow-specific evaluation sets and a calibrated chat evaluation harness. Measure whether the work is useful, as well as whether the run completed.
Experiment tracking. Record the intended outcome of a change, the metric, and the measurement window, then compare it with what happened.
More control. Let projects choose which eligible workflow decisions can run automatically. Make private workflow authoring and upgrades easier.
Easier operation. Add deployment options that reduce dependence on the current managed services, plus notifications that bring people back when a run needs attention.

requirements.text: Complete the browser login when prompted.
For an existing connection that needs authentication, use codex mcp login tin.
Private code schedules reuse saved workflow scheduling; paid occurrences need standing spending authority.
A clean-clone acceptance run and usable .env.example are still outstanding; see self-hosting limits.
Customer billing is optional when self-hosting.
